turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Kia ora, thanks for calling Acme Life, you're speaking with Ravi. Just so you know before we go any further, this call is recorded for quality and training purposes. Who have I got on the line?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Yeah, gidday. Jack here. I saw your ad on Facebook for life cover, figured I'd ring and see what the catch is.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Ha, fair enough, Jack. Happy to walk you through it. Before I look at anything specific for you, can I just confirm your full name and date of birth?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Jack Robert Wilson. Fourteenth of March, 1984.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Thanks Jack, that's Jack Robert Wilson, born 14 March 1984. All good. So, what's got you thinking about life cover at the moment?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: I'm self-employed, sparky. Got my own van, my own gear. Missus works part-time, we've got two kids, eight and eleven. If I fell off a ladder tomorrow there's no work insurance or anything coming through, it's just me.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Right, so you're the main earner and there's no employer scheme sitting behind you. Have you got a mortgage or any big debts you'd want cleared?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Mortgage is about four-twenty left. Bit on the van, maybe fifteen grand. That's about it.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: And any existing life cover at all, through KiwiSaver or a bank policy?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Nah. Nothing. That's sort of why I'm ringing.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Okay. And what would you want the payout to do, mainly? Clear the mortgage, or leave something extra for the family on top?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Clear the house, mainly. Then a bit of a buffer so she's not scrambling. I don't want to be paying through the nose though.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Understood. Any health stuff I should know about? Smoker, ongoing conditions, anything you're on medication for?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Don't smoke. I'm on blood pressure tablets, have been for about three years. Doc says it's under control.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Good to know, thanks. So with Acme Life Cover you can pick anything from fifty thousand up to a million dollars. Based on the mortgage, the van and a buffer for the family, I'd suggest looking at around five hundred thousand. That clears the four-twenty, the van, and leaves roughly sixty-odd thousand for your partner and the kids.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Right. And the blood pressure, is that gonna be a problem? Because that's the sort of thing these outfits use to wriggle out of paying.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: No, you're fine there. Something like blood pressure that's already managed is covered from day one, so you don't need to worry about that.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Huh. Okay. What's that gonna cost me then, the five hundred?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: For you, at forty, non-smoker, five hundred thousand cover comes out at fifty-eight dollars a month.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: And that stays at fifty-eight?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: No, I'll be straight with you on that. The premiums are stepped, so they go up each year as you get older. Fifty-eight is what you'd pay now, and it'll rise a bit each year at renewal.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Right. At least you said it. What else does it do, apart from pay out if I cark it?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: There's a terminal illness benefit as well. If you were diagnosed with less than twelve months to live, the payout comes early, so you'd have it while you're still here to sort things out with the family.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Yeah, that's decent. Look, it sounds alright, but I'd want to talk to the missus and maybe sleep on it. I'll give you a bell back later in the week.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: I hear you, Jack, but honestly I'd hate for you to miss out. That fifty-eight dollar rate is one I can only hold on this call. If you ring back later in the week it'll go through as a fresh quote and it won't be the same number.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Why would it change in a few days? I'm not getting older by Friday.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: It's just how the pricing works on these offers, it's tied to today. And to be honest, talking it over usually just ends up with people putting it off and the family's still sitting there with no cover. You've already told me exactly what you need.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Hmm. I don't love being rushed, mate.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Totally get that. And just so you know, there's a thirty-day free-look period. If you and your partner go through it and decide it's not for you, you cancel within thirty days and get a full refund. So you're not locked in.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Full refund, no fees, nothing?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Full refund within the thirty days, yep.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Alright. Go on then, let's do it.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Great. Before I finalise, let me run through it so we're both clear. It's Acme Life Cover for Jack Robert Wilson, five hundred thousand dollars of cover. It pays out on death, and early if you're diagnosed with a terminal illness with less than twelve months to live. The premium is fifty-eight dollars a month to start, and it's stepped, so it goes up each year with your age. You've got a thirty-day free-look period with a full refund. Are you happy to go ahead on that basis?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Yeah. Yes, go ahead.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Perfect. I'll get the direct debit set up next. Do you want it coming out on a particular day of the month?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: The twentieth. That's after most of my invoices get paid.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Twentieth it is. You'll get the policy documents by email within the next day or so, and the thirty days starts from when you receive them. Have a read through with your partner.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Will do. Cheers, Ravi.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Cheers Jack, thanks for your time. Take care on those ladders.
